content: The following text provides a detailed overview of various studies, guidelines, and expert contributions related to the management of chronic pain in children, as well as the ethical and human rights considerations surrounding healthcare practices. 1. A 2008 article in the BMJ discusses the process of rating the quality of evidence and the strength of recommendations in healthcare decision-making. 2. Lewin et al. (2018) introduced the GRADE-CERQual approach for synthesizing qualitative evidence in healthcare, published in Implementation Science. 3. The Cochrane Pain, Palliative, and Supportive Care Group, led by E. Fisher, conducted a systematic review on the effectiveness and safety of pharmacological, physical, and psychological interventions for managing chronic pain in children. 4. Another review by the same group, led by E. France, focused on qualitative evidence synthesis for managing chronic pain in children (September 2020). 5. Hawkins J. performed an economic analysis of chronic pain management in children, emphasizing cost-effectiveness. 6. Alonso-Coello et al. (2016) developed the GRADE Evidence to Decision (EtD) frameworks, a systematic and transparent method for making informed healthcare choices, published in the BMJ. 7. Palermo et al. (2020) highlighted the importance of measuring and reporting adverse events in clinical trials of psychological treatments for chronic pain, published in Pain. 8. Evans et al. (2016) evaluated the cost-effectiveness of intensive interdisciplinary pediatric chronic pain rehabilitation, published in the Journal of Pediatric Psychology. 9. Lalouni et al. examined the clinical and cost-effectiveness of online cognitive behavioral therapy for children with functional abdominal pain disorders, published in Clinical Gastroenterology and Hepatology. 10. Law et al. (2018) assessed the impact of adjunctive internet-delivered cognitive-behavioral therapy on healthcare costs for adolescents with chronic pain, published in The Journal of Pain. The guidelines also reference key human rights documents, including: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights (1948). The International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights (1966). The Convention Against Torture and Other Cruel, Inhuman, or Degrading Treatment or Punishment (1984). The Convention on the Rights of the Child (2020). The World Health Organization (WHO) guidelines on managing chronic pain in children were developed with contributions from experts worldwide. The guideline development group included professionals from diverse regions and disciplines, such as pediatrics, palliative care, pharmacology, psychology, and human rights law. Systematic reviews were conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of various interventions, including physical therapy, psychological therapy, and pharmacological treatments. These reviews were led by experts such as Dr. Emma Fisher and Dr. Emma France. Additionally, economic evaluations were performed to assess the cost-effectiveness of these interventions, led by Dr. James Hawkins.
